title: Writing Memos and Letters
summary: A memo (memorandum) is a brief written message for internal communication within an organisation — from one department or person to another — to share information, updates or instructions. It is written on plain paper or a memo form, not on a letterhead.

Structure: heading (MEMO/MEMORANDUM, date, To, From, Subject); opening — the purpose; body — details, background and action required, often in points; closing — summary of action needed and signature (Sd/-).
How to write: state the subject clearly; come to the point at once; short, simple, direct sentences (personal pronouns are fine); break the message into points; be brief — the reader is busy.

A letter is a formal or informal written message, often to people outside the organisation. Structure: sender's address, date, recipient's address, subject (in formal letters), salutation, body (introduction, main content, conclusion), complimentary close (Yours sincerely/faithfully), signature and name, enclosures.

Letter of complaint: state the complaint clearly and politely without blaming; give references (order/invoice numbers, dates) and details of the defect; attach or mention evidence; say exactly what you want done (replacement, refund, repair).
Letter of enquiry: ask for specific information; quote references of earlier letters or agreements; make the urgency clear.
Letters go on a letterhead and are written in an indirect, formal style, often outside the organisation; memos go on plain paper or a memo form, are direct and are for internal use.

sa2: What is a memo? For what purpose is it generally used?
A memo is a short, informal written message sent within an organisation in place of a letter. It is used to give information, instructions or updates from one department or person to another.
What points should one keep in mind while writing a memo?
State the subject clearly, come straight to the point, use short and simple sentences, break the message into points and keep it brief, since the reader may be busy.
Write any two differences between a letter and a memo.

A letter is usually for people outside the organisation and is written on a letterhead in a formal, indirect style; a memo is for internal communication, written on plain paper or a memo form in a direct style.
What should a letter of complaint contain?

References (order/invoice number and date), a clear and polite statement of the problem with details of the defect, any evidence, and a clear request for the action wanted, such as replacement or refund.
la4: Imagine you are the Manager of Green Valley Restaurant, Chennai. You ordered 20 cartons of fruit juice from Menu Enterprises, Bengaluru but received 20 cartons of soft drinks. Write a letter of complaint and request a replacement.

Green Valley Restaurant
12, Anna Salai, Chennai
5 March 2026

The Sales Manager
Menu Enterprises
Bengaluru

Subject: Wrong supply against our order

Dear Sir,
We placed an order for 20 cartons of fruit juice (Order No. GVR/26/14 dated 20 February 2026). The consignment received on 3 March, however, contains 20 cartons of soft drinks.
We do not serve soft drinks and cannot accept these goods. Kindly arrange to collect them at your cost and send the 20 cartons of fruit juice within a week, as our stock is running low.
We look forward to your prompt action.
Yours faithfully,
R. Kumar
Manager

Imagine you are the Head of the Student Council and need to inform fellow students about a Cyber Safety Awareness Workshop. Write a memo announcing the event, including the date, time, location and preparations.

MEMORANDUM
Date: 10 March 2026
To: All students, Classes IX–XII
From: Head, Student Council
Subject: Cyber Safety Awareness Workshop

A Cyber Safety Awareness Workshop will be held as follows:
1. Date and time: 18 March 2026, 10 a.m. to 1 p.m.
2. Venue: School Auditorium
3. Topics: strong passwords, suspicious links, protecting personal data, responsible social media use
Please bring a notebook and pen, and note down any questions about online safety beforehand. Attendance is compulsory.
Sd/-
Head, Student Council
